short: An English poet and intellectual who served under the Commonwealth and authored the epic masterpiece Paradise Lost.
full:
John Milton was a towering figure of English literature and a passionate republican intellectual. Born in London, he received an extensive classical education and initially focused on poetry and scholarly pursuits. As the political climate deteriorated in the 1640s, Milton dedicated himself to writing fiercely polemical prose, defending civil and religious liberties, arguing against press censorship, and justifying the execution of Charles I. This work earned him the position of Secretary for Foreign Tongues under Oliver Cromwell's Commonwealth, where he served as the republic's chief propagandist.

The Restoration of the monarchy in 1660 proved catastrophic for Milton; he was briefly imprisoned, stripped of his wealth, and forced into hiding. Completely blind and politically defeated, he dictatated his greatest work, *Paradise Lost* (1667), to assistants. The blank-verse epic recounting the biblical fall of man is widely considered the greatest poem in the English language. He followed it with *Paradise Regained* and the tragedy *Samson Agonistes*, cementing a literary legacy that profoundly influenced Romanticism and subsequent generations of English writers.
